status: approved
buttonLabel: "Learn more about extending your tour on the Riviera Maya"
lead: >-
  The Riviera Maya is an ideal place to extend a journey after exploring Mexico's archaeological sites and cities. The short Southern Adventure tour offers an optional transfer from Cancún to a hotel on the coast or in Tulum for $30 per person. Compare this option with itineraries that already include the Riviera Maya in their main route.
---

## How to add the Riviera Maya to your trip through Mexico

The [Riviera Maya](/mexico/place/riviera-maya/) stretches along the Caribbean Sea on the eastern side of the Yucatán Peninsula. After visiting archaeological sites, historic towns, and natural areas, you can plan some separate beach days here. Depending on your chosen tour, this may mean arranging an additional transfer or visiting a destination already included on the main itinerary.

This collection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} where the Riviera Maya is an optional addition. The [six-day Southern Adventure tour](/mexico/tour/southern-mexico-short-adventure/) normally ends in [Cancún](/mexico/place/cancun/). After the cultural portion, a separate transfer is offered to a hotel on the Riviera Maya or in [Tulum](/mexico/place/tulum/).

## What is included in the short itinerary, and what can be added?

The main Southern Adventure route begins in Chiapas and includes [Sumidero Canyon](/mexico/place/sumidero-canyon/), San Cristóbal de las Casas, [Palenque](/mexico/place/palenque/), and [Campeche](/mexico/place/campeche/). After [Uxmal](/mexico/place/uxmal/) and [Chichén Itzá](/mexico/place/chichen-itza/), travelers arrive in Cancún.

This tour offers **a transfer to a hotel on the Riviera Maya or in Tulum for $30 per person**. This amount applies to the transport option on this particular tour.

| Where to finish | Conditions |
|---|---|
| Cancún | Standard finishing point |
| Riviera Maya | Transfer +$30/person |
| Tulum | Transfer +$30/person |

Paying extra for this transfer does not mean that additional hotel nights, meals, or coastal excursions have been purchased. Decide on the accommodation address in advance: the Riviera Maya covers a large coastal area, and travel times to different hotels vary considerably.

## Choosing a resort for an extended stay

**[Playa del Carmen](/mexico/place/playa-del-carmen/)** is convenient if you want to combine beach time with walks around a resort town and trips across Yucatán.

**[Tulum](/mexico/place/tulum/)** suits travelers interested in beaches, cenotes, and Maya ruins overlooking the sea. However, a transfer to a hotel in Tulum and a tour of its archaeological zone are separate services. Arranging the transfer does not confirm that admission to the ruins has been paid for.

**Other Riviera Maya hotels** can be chosen according to location, beach access, the level of privacy you want, and your onward flight. Compare the exact address, excursion logistics, and accommodation conditions rather than relying exclusively on the name of the coastline.

## When is the coast already included in the main route?

The final day of the [12-day Viva Mexico program](/mexico/tour/viva-mexico/) continues to the Riviera Maya after [Chichén Itzá](/mexico/place/chichen-itza/) and [Valladolid](/mexico/place/valladolid/). The coast is part of the main itinerary, but the subsequent overnight stay is not included.

On the [8-day Mexico Lindo trip](/mexico/tour/mexico-lindo-eight-days/), traveling to the Riviera Maya is likewise part of the main day. The final transfer allows drop-off in Cancún, Playa del Carmen, or the town of Tulum; accommodation on the Caribbean coast is charged separately.

This distinction matters when comparing programs. On the short Southern Adventure, you need to add a transfer to your chosen hotel. On the other two itineraries, the journey to the coast is already included, but any extra nights by the sea still need to be arranged separately.

## How much time to spend by the sea?

If you want to relax after busy days of sightseeing, plan dedicated nights on the coast rather than trying to visit beaches and cenotes immediately after a lengthy drive. For each excursion, check the journey from your hotel and the rules for visiting the chosen attraction.

It helps to connect the tour's final destination with your return flight early in the planning process: decide on the departure city and airport, your hotel, check-out date, and transfer time. When comparing [tours in Mexico](/mexico/tour/), look not only at overall duration but also at the endpoint, included transport, and number of paid hotel nights.

## Frequently asked questions about extending a trip on the Riviera Maya

### Can I reach the Riviera Maya after Southern Adventure?

Yes. The six-day tour offers an additional transfer to a hotel on the Riviera Maya or in Tulum for $30 per person.

### What does the $30 cover?

It is the price of the optional transfer. It does not mean accommodation, a beach holiday package, or a sightseeing tour of Tulum is included.

### Is the Riviera Maya included on Viva Mexico?

Yes, as a main destination on the final day. However, an overnight stay after the tour ends is not included, and an extension is arranged separately.

### Which is better for a holiday, Cancún or Tulum?

The choice depends on your hotel's address, how long you have for leisure, and your return flight. Cancún is the main endpoint of the short itinerary; Tulum can be selected when arranging an extension.

buttonLabel: "Explore tours visiting the Riviera Maya"
lead: >-
  The Riviera Maya is often the final stop on a journey through Mexico: after Chichén Itzá, cenotes, and Yucatán's towns, the route reaches the Caribbean Sea. But a transfer to the coast, an excursion to Tulum, and a stay at a beach hotel are different services. Compare our current itineraries and learn when to plan seaside relaxation separately.
---

## How the Riviera Maya fits into tours of Mexico

The [Riviera Maya](/mexico/place/riviera-maya/) stretches along the Caribbean coast of Quintana Roo state. Beaches, coastal towns, and monuments of Maya civilization sit close together here. It is a convenient place to finish a journey after [Mérida](/mexico/place/merida/), [Chichén Itzá](/mexico/place/chichen-itza/), and other historic sites on the Yucatán Peninsula: the sightseeing portion ends, and the remaining days can be spent by the sea.

Our collection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} that visit the Riviera Maya or finish in this area. **The most important distinction is exactly what the paid tour includes.** Mentioning a coastal region in an itinerary does not mean nights at a beach hotel are included. Some programs provide a transfer to the coast; others offer an optional additional transfer or a longer stay.

If several days at the beach are your main goal, first decide how many nights you want after the sightseeing itinerary, then choose the tour. For travelers more interested in Maya heritage and Mexican towns, the order is reversed: choose the route first and add beach days if desired.

## Four Riviera Maya routes and an option with a separate transfer

### Eight days: Mexico City, Yucatán, and a transfer to the coast

[Mexico Lindo: 8 days from Mexico City to the Caribbean coast](/mexico/tour/mexico-lindo-eight-days/) begins with the capital's historic center, Teotihuacán, and Xochimilco. After flying to Mérida, the itinerary includes Uxmal, Kabah, cenotes, and Chichén Itzá. On the final day, drop-off is offered at one of three destinations: Cancún, Playa del Carmen, or the town of Tulum.

**Accommodation on the Riviera Maya is not included in the eight-day program.** It can be arranged separately. The domestic flight from Mexico City to Mérida is also charged separately. This itinerary suits travelers who want a sightseeing journey and the freedom to decide how long to spend at the beach afterward.

### Twelve days: the capital, Oaxaca, and Yucatán

[Viva Mexico](/mexico/tour/viva-mexico/) combines 12 days in Mexico City, Oaxaca, and Yucatán. It devotes more time to culture: [Monte Albán](/mexico/place/monte-alban/), artisan workshops, Mitla, Uxmal, and cenotes. The final day passes through Chichén Itzá and Valladolid before continuing toward the coast.

The program expressly states that **the overnight stay after arriving on the Riviera Maya is not included**, although an extension is possible. This option suits travelers who prioritize crafts and archaeology over the number of days at the beach.

### Six days: historic sites and a short seaside ending

[Grand Mexico Holiday](/mexico/tour/grand-mexico-holiday/) takes travelers through key attractions of Yucatán and finishes around Cancún and the Riviera Maya. The main itinerary lasts 6 days. It suits those who want to visit several archaeological sites on one trip without stretching the journey to two weeks.

The [Cancún, Tulum, Palenque, Uxmal and Chichén Itzá tour](/mexico/tour/mexico-cancun-tulum-palenque-uxmal-chichen-itza/) also lasts 6 days, but has a different focus: Tulum, Palenque, Calakmul, Uxmal, and Chichén Itzá. It ends with a transfer to a hotel in Cancún or on the Riviera Maya, or to the airport. Beach time after the sightseeing portion must be arranged separately.

**Outside the main collection there is an itinerary with an optional transfer:** [Southern Adventure — Short Itinerary](/mexico/tour/southern-mexico-short-adventure/) starts in Chiapas, visiting Sumidero Canyon, San Cristóbal de las Casas, and Palenque, followed by Campeche, Uxmal, and Mérida. The final stops are Chichén Itzá and Cancún. Under this tour's terms, an additional transfer to a hotel on the Riviera Maya or in Tulum is charged separately. This is central to any comparison: the main route includes Cancún, but reaching a specific coastal hotel may require an additional service.

## Comparing the current tours

| If your priority is | Start with |
|---|---|
| Mexico City sightseeing | Mexico Lindo, 8 days |
| Oaxaca's artisan workshops | Viva Mexico, 12 days |
| Palenque and southern Mexico | Southern Adventure, 6 days |
| Yucatán archaeology | Grand Mexico Holiday, 6 days |
| Tulum and Calakmul | Cancún, Tulum, Palenque, 6 days |

All five programs can be compared individually using the links above. The table below lists four tours that include the Riviera Maya on their main itinerary; on Southern Adventure, the transfer to the coast is an additional paid option:

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_mexico_lindo_eight_days,tour_source_viva_meksika,tour_source_bolshie_meksikanskie_kanikuly,tour_source_cancun_palenque_cenot}}

## Where to end your journey: Cancún, Playa del Carmen, or Tulum

The Riviera Maya has several visitor centers, and the best choice depends on your plans afterward. [Cancún](/mexico/place/cancun/) is convenient for travelers finishing their journey via an international airport. Playa del Carmen is often chosen for a stay in a lively town with a beach, restaurants, and opportunities for day trips. [Tulum](/mexico/place/tulum/) combines the coast with archaeological monuments.

However, "drop-off in the town of Tulum" and "a transfer directly to Tulum's Hotel Zone" are not always equivalent. For example, Mexico Lindo excludes transport to Tulum's Hotel Zone from its base terms. When booking, compare the transfer endpoint with your chosen hotel's exact address.

The same applies to the coast after Chichén Itzá. A tour can finish in one town, with an overnight stay or transfer to a neighboring resort treated as a separate extension. The more precisely the final destination is specified, the fewer unnecessary transfers you will need.

## When to plan your beach extension

The Caribbean coast is warm throughout the year, but the quality of a beach holiday depends on rainfall, wind, and sea conditions. The official Atlantic tropical cyclone season runs **from June 1 to November 30**; that is a period of seasonal risk, not a prediction of a storm on any particular date. During wetter months, allow flexibility for changing weather, especially if boat outings and marine activities are added to sightseeing.

In addition to weather, consider actual distances between the tour's endpoint, your hotel, and the airport. If you plan an evening flight after the final excursion, check the driving time and expected arrival. If you want time to relax by the sea, separate hotel nights make more sense than trying to fit a beach visit and departure into the same day.

For more resort options, explore [beach holidays in Mexico](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/mexico/), or visit the [Mexico tour catalog](/mexico/tour/) to compare sightseeing itineraries.

## Frequently asked questions about tours visiting the Riviera Maya

### Do all tours in this selection include a beach hotel?

No. Some itineraries finish with a transfer to the coast. On Mexico Lindo and Viva Mexico, accommodation on the Riviera Maya after the sightseeing program is not part of the base package. Check the terms of your chosen tour.

### Can I finish sightseeing in Cancún but stay in Tulum?

You can plan that as an extension. However, a transfer from the tour's endpoint to the specific hotel and additional nights may be charged separately. Mentioning Tulum in the route does not change this.

### Which itinerary should I choose if I am interested in both Oaxaca and beaches?

Viva Mexico combines Oaxaca, its artisan communities, and Yucatán's archaeological attractions with an ending on the Riviera Maya. Beach time after the 12-day program is arranged separately.

### Is there an itinerary shorter than a week?

Yes. The collection contains six-day tours. Their primary focus is sightseeing, so the number of beach nights must be considered separately.

### Can I add several days by the sea after Chichén Itzá?

For itineraries finishing at the coast, this is a logical extension. First confirm the transfer endpoint, then choose accommodation, and only afterward plan any additional excursions.

## San Ángel in Mexico City: crafts, squares, and historic streets

**San Ángel** is located in the south of [Mexico City](/mexico/place/mexico-city-and-teotihuacan/). It is a historic neighborhood of cobbled lanes, colonial houses, and squares. Travelers interested in small galleries, crafts, and unhurried walks particularly enjoy visiting.

San Ángel is very different from the city center around the [Zócalo](/mexico/place/mexico-city-zocalo/). Instead of large government buildings, you will find colorful façades, wooden doors, courtyards, and old churches. For a first visit, a walking route through several adjacent streets works well.

## Plaza San Jacinto and the old neighborhoods

**Plaza San Jacinto** is one of the area's most recognizable locations. Historic buildings surround the square, and cultural venues operate nearby. Start your walk here and then explore the adjoining streets, taking in the architecture and small courtyards.

The historic buildings recall a period when this part of modern Mexico City developed separately from the central districts. San Ángel still feels like a small town, even though it is now part of a huge capital.

Choose comfortable footwear for your walk: the cobblestones can be uneven, and some sections become slippery after rain.

## The Saturday market: Bazar Sábado

**Bazar Sábado** is a well-known artisan market near Plaza San Jacinto. According to Mexico City's tourism portal, it has operated since the 1960s, bringing together artists, designers, and craftspeople.

You can find jewelry, ceramics, textiles, wooden objects, and other handmade pieces for sale. It is an opportunity to see many different Mexican artistic traditions in one place.

The crucial detail is that the market takes place on **Saturdays**. You can walk through San Ángel on other days, but do not expect the same stalls or artisans to be there throughout the week.

| When you visit | What to enjoy |
|---|---|
| Saturday | Artisan market |
| Weekday | Streets and galleries |
| A few hours | A historic walk |

Check current schedules for market spaces and museums before your visit.

## What crafts to look for

At the market and neighboring galleries, you may see pottery, silverwork, paintings, textiles, and wooden objects. When buying souvenirs, it is worth asking about the maker and production process. Not every piece bearing a traditional design was made by a local artisan.

San Ángel is especially convenient because its markets and galleries sit among historic city architecture. You can explore a few workshops, head to the square, and continue your walk through the neighborhood.

For a more in-depth experience of crafts beyond the capital, consider [San Antonio Arrazola](/mexico/place/san-antonio-arrazola/) and [San Bartolo Coyotepec](/mexico/place/san-bartolo-coyotepec/) in Oaxaca state. These are separate artisan towns with different traditions, and reaching them requires a journey to another part of Mexico.

## What else to see beyond the market

The neighborhood contains the historic former El Carmen monastery complex, linked to San Ángel's colonial past. The older streets are home to churches, smaller cultural spaces, and squares with restaurants.

You can choose one museum visit and leave more time for exploring the streets. This keeps the walk rewarding even when some exhibitions are closed.

San Ángel is often associated with nearby [Coyoacán](/mexico/place/coyoacan/), known for its colonial architecture and Frida Kahlo's history. The two neighborhoods complement each other but are separate: allow time for the transfer.

## Getting here from central Mexico City

San Ángel lies in the southern part of the city, so journey time depends on traffic. For a sightseeing day, choose the starting and finishing points of your walk in advance.

If the market is on your itinerary, set aside time for it, especially on a weekend. For an independent visit, identify the particular square you need rather than searching only for the broad name San Ángel, which covers different streets and transport access points.

You can combine the walk with cultural attractions in southern districts, but trying to fit in the northern [Basilica of Guadalupe](/mexico/place/basilica-of-guadalupe/) and distant Teotihuacán within the same few hours is impractical.

## San Ángel on Ada Tours itineraries

San Ángel features on the [12-day Viva Mexico tour](/mexico/tour/viva-mexico/) as part of the introduction to the capital. It is one of the historical and cultural stops before the journey continues through Mexico.

When choosing the itinerary, check which day includes the visit, whether the artisan market is open, and how much time remains for other attractions. A visit outside Saturday can still be rewarding, but the experience will differ. Browse the programs in our [Mexico tour catalog](/mexico/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about San Ángel

### On which day is the famous market held?

Bazar Sábado is a Saturday market. Check the organizers' website for the latest schedule.

### Is San Ángel in central Mexico City?

It is a historic neighborhood in the city's south, separate from the central Zócalo square.

### Is San Ángel worth visiting when the market is closed?

Yes. Historic streets, squares, and individual galleries are still worth exploring.

### Can I combine San Ángel with Coyoacán?

Yes, if you arrange transport in advance and leave enough time for both neighborhoods.

## Tours visiting San Ángel: which journey should you choose?

[San Ángel](/mexico/place/san-angel/) lies in southern Mexico City. Historic buildings, cobbled streets, Plaza San Jacinto, and the craftwork for which the neighborhood has been known for generations make it worth visiting. It is a welcome addition to a broader tour of the capital: after museums, archaeological sites, and busy avenues, you can stroll among low-rise houses and art workshops.

Our catalog features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} including San Ángel on the main route. **This is the [12-day Viva Mexico: Mexico City, Oaxaca and Yucatán tour](/mexico/tour/viva-mexico/).** The neighborhood is visited on day 4 alongside [Xochimilco](/mexico/place/xochimilco/) and [Coyoacán](/mexico/place/coyoacan/). The journey then continues through Oaxaca and Yucatán's monuments. San Ángel is therefore part of a wider introduction to Mexico, not a standalone weekend in the neighborhood.

When choosing a tour, examine the stops on the specific day rather than only the overall trip length. These three southern Mexico City destinations offer a combination of urban neighborhoods and Xochimilco's canals, but the time available for markets and galleries depends on the agreed itinerary.

## What you may see during the San Ángel stop

The main walking area centers on Plaza San Jacinto and adjoining streets. Colorful façades, old doors, courtyards, and cobblestones are typical features. The area has galleries and small shops showing work by Mexican artisans. It is better to leave some free time for a few streets than try to see the entire south of Mexico City in an hour.

**Bazar Sábado**, an artisan market near Plaza San Jacinto, is a particular attraction. Held on Saturdays, it sells ceramics, textiles, jewelry, wooden items, and contemporary works by artists. It is worthwhile if your stop really falls on a Saturday and leaves time to browse the stalls. On other days, the neighborhood remains attractive, but the Saturday stalls should not be expected.

The Viva Mexico itinerary includes **a visit to San Ángel as a destination**, not a guaranteed visit to a particular market, workshop, or gallery. Ada Tours can help set priorities for the day, but check the actual schedule before selecting your departure.

## San Ángel, Coyoacán and Xochimilco in one day

These three stops are all in the southern part of the metropolitan area and complement each other.

| Place | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| [San Ángel](/mexico/place/san-angel/) | Historic streets and crafts |
| [Coyoacán](/mexico/place/coyoacan/) | Squares and urban culture |
| [Xochimilco](/mexico/place/xochimilco/) | Canals and boats |

All three are included on day 4 of Viva Mexico. A separate [Xochimilco and Southern Mexico City excursion](/mexico/xochimilco/xochimilco-south-mexico-city-tour/) also covers these areas. If the market in San Ángel is your main interest, discuss in advance how much time to devote to it and which other stops might have to be shortened.

**The day of the week matters.** The 12-day itinerary offers departures beginning on Wednesdays and Fridays. Counting in the usual way, day 4 would therefore fall on a Saturday or Monday, respectively. However, the sequence of visits, workshop availability, and travel dates must be confirmed for the specific departure: the market's schedule does not automatically become a guaranteed part of the tour.

## Who should choose a tour with San Ángel?

This is a good option for travelers interested in urban history, art, and everyday Mexican culture. San Ángel is a compact cultural stop within a much larger journey. Most of the 12-day itinerary takes place well beyond the capital: in [Oaxaca](/mexico/place/oaxaca/), travelers explore crafts and archaeology before continuing to Yucatán's monuments.

If you want to learn more about crafts, consider other stops in the published itinerary: [San Antonio Arrazola](/mexico/place/san-antonio-arrazola/), known for wooden alebrijes, and [San Bartolo Coyotepec](/mexico/place/san-bartolo-coyotepec/), known for black pottery. These are separate towns in Oaxaca state and a different stage of the journey.

Viva Mexico includes 12 days and 11 nights, hotel accommodation with breakfast, shared transfers and excursions, a bilingual guide, and admission to historical sites. Domestic and international flights are excluded. Full terms, dates, and pricing are available in the [tour description](/mexico/tour/viva-mexico/) and matter more than the general impression from the catalog.

{{#if catalog.hasComparableUsdPrice}}
For budget comparisons, you can use the catalog's calculated starting price: {{catalog.minUsdPriceLabel}}. Verify the price basis and room category on the program page.
{{/if}}

## Practical questions about visiting San Ángel on a tour

### Can I visit Bazar Sábado on any day?

No. This is a Saturday market. When planning, check that your stop falls on Saturday and that you will have time to visit. Walks around the neighborhood are possible on other days, but individual galleries have their own opening schedules.

### Is San Ángel a separate tour or part of an itinerary?

In this selection, it is a stop on the [12-day Viva Mexico program](/mexico/tour/viva-mexico/). It is combined with Coyoacán and Xochimilco on one day, while the overall route covers several regions.

### Can I arrange a longer walk through the neighborhood?

Discuss this when finalizing the trip. Spending more time in San Ángel means changing the order or duration of other stops that day; no additional service is included without confirmation.

### How is San Ángel different from Oaxaca's artisan villages?

San Ángel offers city streets, galleries, and a market. In [Arrazola](/mexico/place/san-antonio-arrazola/), you can see wooden figures carved and painted, while [Coyotepec](/mexico/place/san-bartolo-coyotepec/) is known for black pottery. These visits complement rather than repeat one another.

### Where can I see all the main tours of Mexico?

Start with the [Mexico tour catalog](/mexico/tour/), then open individual programs to compare durations, destinations, and included services. Cultural itineraries are also listed among the [cultural and historical tours of Mexico](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/mexico/).

## San Antonio Arrazola: where wooden alebrijes are created

**San Antonio Arrazola lies near [Oaxaca](/mexico/place/oaxaca/), at the foot of the [Monte Albán](/mexico/place/monte-alban/) area.** The village is known for artisans who carve brightly colored wooden figures of animals and fantastical creatures. These are called alebrijes.

The opportunity to watch people working by hand is the main attraction. An artisan begins with wood, gradually shapes the piece, then applies tiny painted patterns. A finished figure may be covered in hundreds of colored lines and dots.

## Where the Arrazola tradition began

Oaxaca state's official tourism portal links the development of local wooden alebrijes to artisan **Manuel Jiménez**. Later, the craft spread among family workshops. Today, Arrazola residents create figures valued far beyond the region.

It is important, however, to distinguish the original urban papier-mâché alebrije tradition from Oaxaca's wood carving. They use different materials and represent distinct artistic traditions, although contemporary tourism often uses the same name for both.

Arrazola figures are usually carved from copal wood and painted by hand. Each artisan chooses their own subjects, colors, and decorative techniques.

## How alebrijes are made

First, the basic shape of an animal or fantastical creature is carved from a block of wood. The figure is then sanded and prepared for painting. Finally, colored paint, dots, and fine lines are applied.

In a workshop, you may see different stages side by side: unworked wood, a carved but unpainted piece, and a completed colorful figure. This comparison makes the work involved in the craft apparent.

| Stage | What happens |
|---|---|
| Carving | The figure takes shape |
| Preparation | The surface is sanded |
| Painting | Colors and patterns are applied |
| Finished piece | The result is displayed |

Tools and techniques vary from one workshop to another. Do not assume every artisan uses exactly the same method or promise that every visitor will be allowed to make a figure themselves.

## What kinds of figures are there?

Alebrijes include familiar animals—cats, birds, dogs, and jaguars—as well as fantastical characters. Some combine features of several animals. The maker chooses the subject; it does not necessarily represent an ancient mythical being.

Brightly colored patterns make even small figures expressive. Some workshops use extremely fine brushes, building their designs from repeated dots and lines.

If you want to buy a figure, ask about the maker, materials, time needed to produce it, and packing requirements. Delicate projecting parts may need careful handling during travel.

## What happens on a workshop visit?

On a good artisan excursion, meeting the maker and learning about the process matter more than a quick stop at a souvenir shop. You may see carving and painting, hear about the family's craft history, and discuss why prices vary between figures.

Arrange the visit ahead of time if you want to see an active workshop rather than just a retail outlet. Opportunities to speak with an artisan, take photographs, and watch specific techniques depend on the arrangements.

Arrazola is near other cultural sites in the valley, so it does not require a separate multi-day journey devoted solely to the village. A more detailed workshop class, however, needs additional time.

## Arrazola, Monte Albán, and black pottery

The same region is home to **[Monte Albán](/mexico/place/monte-alban/)**, a Zapotec archaeological center. It can be combined with an artisan itinerary when transport and time allow.

Another artisan village is **[San Bartolo Coyotepec](/mexico/place/san-bartolo-coyotepec/)**, known for barro negro black pottery. Comparing the 2 stops shows the use of very different materials: wood and paint in Arrazola, clay and firing in Coyotepec.

Allow time at each workshop to see how the pieces are made. A quick shopping stop offers far less insight.

## San Antonio Arrazola on Ada Tours itineraries

Arrazola features on the [12-day Viva Mexico tour](/mexico/tour/viva-mexico/) and the [five-day Oaxaca short getaway](/mexico/tour/oaxaca-city-break-5-days/). These trips differ in their overall geography and the time spent in Oaxaca state.

When choosing, check the format of the workshop visit, which other stops are included, and whether a separate hands-on class is offered. You can explore the full selection in our [Mexico tour catalog](/mexico/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about Arrazola

### What are alebrijes?

Decorative figures of real and fantastical animals. In Arrazola, they are primarily carved from wood and painted by hand.

### Can visitors watch the artisans work?

Yes. Active workshops demonstrate the process of making the figures. Confirm the particular visit arrangements in advance.

### Where is Arrazola located?

Near the city of Oaxaca, close to the Monte Albán archaeological area.

### How is Arrazola different from Coyotepec?

Arrazola is known for wooden alebrijes, while Coyotepec is famous for black pottery.
